svg.title: gpushare: The Memory It Releases and Re-Creates
svg.desc: The CUDA checkpoint API cannot checkpoint a process that maps GPU memory another process exported. For each kind of shared memory, the figure shows what gpushare's release does before the driver checkpoint and what load, remap and resume do after the restore. Allocations are saved to a chunk store and re-created at the same virtual addresses, so pointers and captured CUDA graphs stay valid.
svg.text: gpushare: The Memory It Releases and Re-Creates
Tracked in every process that preloads libnvsnap_gpushare.so; driven by nvsnap-gpu-suspend.
At release, before the driver checkpoint
fresh export, same address, same access
on cuMem memory (2 MiB and up)
the handle the app holds stays valid
Load and remap: re-create or re-import,
rejoin devices; resume binds the memory
Grace, driver 580: the driver restores none
cuMemAlloc of 2 MiB and up; app-shared
Save to the chunk store, then free
Load: re-create at the same address
with the same properties and access
Written once per content (model weights repeat across checkpoints); all-zero chunks are not stored;
each chunk written to a temporary file, flushed, then renamed. Moved into the checkpoint as gpushare/.
Smaller cuMemAlloc memory stays legacy memory. gpushare hands out its own handle for it and makes the driver export only when a peer opens the handle; a handle that is opened stays a legacy
export, which the driver checkpoint cannot handle.
Multicast needs a driver that lets a restored process create and join multicast objects: 610.57.04 on GB300 does, 580.173.02 does not.
